sections.h2: Is there one Oklahoma homestead exemption or two?
sections.html:
There are two separate protections that share a name: a property tax exemption under Title 68 and a creditor protection for the home under Title 31. A seller may have one, both or neither, and they are claimed in different ways.

The tax exemption is a filing with the county assessor that lowers the yearly bill. The Title 31 homestead is not filed anywhere. It is a legal shield that protects a principal residence from forced sale by most creditors, within acreage limits.

sections.h2: What does the property tax homestead exemption take off the bill?
sections.html:
It exempts the first $1,000 of assessed value from ad valorem tax. The Oklahoma County Assessor's office told residents in a 2025 notice that this saves roughly $87 to $141 in that county, so the amount is modest and depends on local millage.

A second $1,000 of assessed value is exempt for a household whose gross income from all sources is $30,000 or less. In Oklahoma County that application is renewed each year until the owner reaches age 65.

sections.h2: What does the state application form ask?
sections.html:
Form 921 asks questions that decide eligibility, and a no to the wrong one can end the claim. The form asks whether any part of the property is rented, whether any is used commercially, whether the owner holds only a partial interest, whether it sits in a trust, and whether the home is a manufactured home.

  • Did you own the property on or before January 1?
  • Did you live in it as your residence on January 1?
  • Will your deed be on record with the county clerk on or before February 1?
  • Do you have, or did you have last year, a homestead exemption elsewhere?

The form warns that an application filed after March 15, or one with a no in the ownership section, may only count toward the following year.

sections.h2: What is the senior valuation limitation, and does it last after a sale?
sections.html:
It locks the taxable fair cash value of the home for an owner who is 65 or older, who is the head of household and whose income is within the HUD qualifying limit. The Tulsa County Assessor lists $90,300 as the limit for the 2026 tax year, while Oklahoma County's 2025 notice cited $89,500, so the number changes by year.

It does not freeze the tax bill itself. Tulsa County says the amount can still rise if the excise board adds millage, a judgment is taken against the county, or voters change assessment percentages.

The limitation ends when title is transferred. A buyer starts fresh, and a seller who is moving does not carry it to the next house automatically.

sections.h2: What must a new owner do after buying a homestead?
sections.html:
A new owner has to apply again. Form 921 states that any purchaser or new owner must file an application, so the seller's exemption does not pass with the deed.

The statute also puts a duty on the seller side: a taxpayer must tell the assessor in writing about a change in use, and recording a deed or other instrument showing a change of ownership counts as sufficient notice. Owners who keep an exemption they no longer qualify for owe twice the unpaid taxes plus interest and penalty, face a lien, and lose the right to a homestead exemption on any Oklahoma property for two years.

sections.h2: What does the Title 31 homestead protect when you sell or owe money?
sections.html:
Under 31 O.S. 2, an urban homestead may not exceed one acre and a rural homestead may not exceed 160 acres. In a city, at least 75 percent of the floor area of the improvements must be the principal residence, and if more than 25 percent is used for business the exemption is capped at $5,000.

Temporary renting does not change the homestead character as long as the owner has not acquired another homestead. Section 31-1 also treats a manufactured home as exempt when it is the owner's principal residence, with no acreage figure stated there.

These rules decide what a judgment creditor can reach when a house is sold, and they are why title companies ask who lives in the home.

sections.h2: Does a spouse have to sign the deed?
sections.html:
Yes in most cases. Under 16 O.S. 4, a deed, mortgage or contract affecting an exempt homestead, other than a lease of one year or less, must be in writing and signed by both spouses if both are living and neither is divorced or legally separated.

  • An agent may sign for a spouse only if the power of attorney is recorded with the county clerk in the county where the property sits.
  • A deed recorded for ten years with no court challenge on homestead grounds is treated as valid without the spouse's signature.
  • Missing a spouse's signature on a VA-insured purchase does not void it.

Sellers who inherited a house or who are separated but not divorced often discover this requirement late in the process.

sections.h2: How do local offices handle homestead filings and fraud?
sections.html:
The Oklahoma County Assessor says filing the exemption is free and warns against companies that charge to prepare and file it. His office reported rejecting 190 applications from a title company that used forms not approved by the Oklahoma Tax Commission.

The county clerk also runs a free deed alert service that notifies an owner by text, phone or email when a document is recorded under their name, which helps spot deed tampering. Oklahoma has 77 counties, and each assessor runs its own filing process, so check the office for the county where the house sits.

The state itself, with about 3.96 million residents in 2020, is large enough that deadlines like March 15 are the same everywhere but the local office hours, online portals and field filing days are not.

sections.h2: How does a homestead claim fit into selling the house quickly?
sections.html:
Homestead status touches three parts of a sale: the tax bill that gets prorated at closing, the spouse's signature on the deed, and whether a creditor has any claim on the proceeds. A seller who has not filed for the exemption can still sell, but may have paid more tax than needed.

If a sale is happening before March 15, the exemption claim can still be filed by the owner who lived there on January 1, and a late claim only counts toward the next year. Because a new owner starts over, the buyer should file promptly after closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for the Oklahoma homestead exemption?
faqs.a: March 15, or within 30 days after a notice of valuation increase, whichever is later. Under Form 921 a later application can still be filed, but it counts from the following tax year.

faqs.q: Do I have to reapply for the homestead exemption every year?
faqs.a: No. A taxpayer who was granted the exemption and still lives in the home does not have to reapply. The additional exemption for households at $30,000 or less is the exception, and in Oklahoma County it is refiled yearly until age 65.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption transfer to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Form 921 states that any purchaser or new owner must file their own application. The senior valuation limitation also ends when title is transferred.

faqs.q: How many acres does an Oklahoma homestead cover?
faqs.a: One acre inside a city or town and 160 acres in a rural area, under 31 O.S. 2. In town, the principal residence must make up at least 75 percent of the improvements to avoid the $5,000 cap.

faqs.q: Is it free to file for the exemption?
faqs.a: Yes with the county assessor. The Oklahoma County Assessor states there is no cost to file and cautions against paying outside companies that charge a preparation fee.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house without my spouse signing?
faqs.a: Generally not if it is your exempt homestead and your spouse is living and not divorced or separated. Section 16-4 requires both signatures, with narrow exceptions such as a recorded power of attorney.
